title: Empirical single-cell tracking and cell-fate simulation reveal dual roles of p53 in tumor suppression.
authors: Rancourt, Ann; Sato, Sachiko; Satoh, Masahiko S
one_liner_zh: 该文通过单细胞追踪和细胞命运模拟研究p53在肿瘤抑制中的双重作用，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: The tumor suppressor p53 regulates various stress responses via increasing its cellular levels. The lowest p53 levels occur in unstressed cells; however, the functions of these low levels remain unclear. To investigate the functions, we used empirical single-cell tracking of p53-expressing (Control) cells and cells in which p53 expression was silenced by RNA interference (p53 RNAi). Here, we show that p53 RNAi cells underwent more frequent cell death and cell fusion, which further induced multipolar cell division to generate aneuploid progeny. Those results suggest that the low levels of p53 in unstressed cells indeed have a role in suppressing the induction of cell death and the formation of aneuploid cells. We further investigated the impact of p53 silencing by developing an algorithm to simulate the fates of individual cells. Simulation of the fate of aneuploid cells revealed that these cells could propagate to create an aneuploid cell population. In addition, the simulation also revealed that more frequent induction of cell death in p53 RNAi cells under unstressed conditions conferred a disadvantage in terms of population expansion compared with Control cells, resulting in faster expansion of Control cells compared with p53 RNAi cells, leading to Control cells predominating in mixed cell populations. In contrast, the expansion of Control cells, but not p53 RNAi cells, was suppressed when the damage response was induced, allowing p53 RNAi cells to expand their population compared with the Control cells. These results suggest that, although p53 could suppress the formation of aneuploid cells, which could have a role in tumorigenesis, it could also allow the expansion of cells lacking p53 expression when the damage response is induced. p53 may thus play a role in both the suppression and the promotion of malignant cell formation during tumorigenesis.
abstract_zh: 肿瘤抑制因子p53通过增加其细胞水平来调控多种应激反应。在未受应激的细胞中，p53水平最低；然而，这些低水平p53的功能仍不清楚。为探究其功能，我们采用了经验性单细胞追踪方法，对表达p53的（对照）细胞以及通过RNA干扰（p53 RNAi）沉默p53表达的细胞进行了研究。在此，我们显示p53 RNAi细胞经历了更频繁的细胞死亡和细胞融合，这进一步诱导了多极细胞分裂，从而产生非整倍体后代。这些结果表明，未受应激细胞中低水平的p53确实在抑制细胞死亡诱导和非整倍体细胞形成中发挥作用。我们进一步通过开发一种算法来模拟单个细胞的命运，以研究p53沉默的影响。对非整倍体细胞命运的模拟显示，这些细胞能够增殖形成非整倍体细胞群体。此外，模拟还揭示，在未受应激条件下，p53 RNAi细胞中更频繁的细胞死亡诱导在群体扩张方面相对于对照细胞构成劣势，导致对照细胞比p53 RNAi细胞扩张更快，从而使对照细胞在混合细胞群体中占优势。相反，当损伤反应被诱导时，对照细胞的扩张受到抑制，而p53 RNAi细胞则不受抑制，使得p53 RNAi细胞相对于对照细胞能够扩大其群体。这些结果表明，尽管p53能抑制可能在肿瘤发生中起作用的非整倍体细胞形成，但在损伤反应诱导时，它也可能允许缺乏p53表达的细胞扩张。因此，p53可能在肿瘤发生过程中既抑制又促进恶性细胞的形成。
